1_purpose_and_scope.purpose: Defines the end-to-end architecture for the Battery-Aware Social Communication Platform and specifies how to build it inside Google Antigravity, an agent-first development platform. It translates the PRD into system boundaries, service contracts, data models, and an agent-executable build plan.
audience: Human engineers needing a reference architecture
AI coding agents (Gemini 3 Pro / Claude Sonnet in Antigravity) using this file as their primary planning artifact
inScope: Mobile client architecture (Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose)
Real-time messaging and WebRTC calling architecture

2_architecture_principles.description: Battery monitoring, call signaling, and media transport are decoupled services so the safety-critical battery logic can be tested and shipped independently.
If the Battery Monitoring module cannot read battery state, the system must never block emergency call visibility or crash the call — it degrades to warning-only mode.
Battery level is device-local; the termination decision is made on-device for zero latency, then reported to the backend for history/analytics.
All Spring Boot services are horizontally scalable and stateless; state lives in PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3 only.
Every service/module is scoped to a single domain so one Antigravity agent task can own it end-to-end, including tests.
Every architectural component maps to an automated test and an Antigravity Artifact (walkthrough, screenshot, or test report).
TLS everywhere, encryption at rest, least-privilege service accounts, and an E2EE path for 1:1 chat.

3_high_level_architecture.description: Layered, microservices-based architecture with a mobile client, an API/real-time gateway layer, domain microservices, and shared data infrastructure.

4_mobile_client_architecture.pattern: Clean Architecture with MVVM presentation layer, Kotlin + Jetpack Compose
4_mobile_client_architecture.rationale: Keeps Battery-Aware Calling logic testable in isolation from Android framework classes.

batteryMonitorModule.implementation: Android Foreground Service, started only when a call begins and stopped the instant the call ends

components.name: CallForegroundService
components.responsibility: Owns the active call lifecycle; hosts the BroadcastReceiver for ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED.

components.name: BatteryMonitorUseCase
components.responsibility: Pure-Kotlin state machine: reads battery %, compares to configured thresholds, emits BatteryState (Normal/Warning/Critical).

components.name: CallTerminationController
components.responsibility: Subscribes to BatteryState; on Critical, releases camera/mic, tears down the WebRTC PeerConnection, and stops the foreground service.

5_battery_aware_calling_system.description: The product's primary innovation, treated as a first-class subsystem with its own state machine, independent of general call-quality logic.

transitions.condition: terminal state — no auto-resume even if battery rises (e.g. charger connected)

sequence_battery_monitoring_during_call: BatteryMonitorUseCase -> Mobile UI: BatteryState.Warning -> WARNING banner shown
CallForegroundService -> WebRTC Engine: stop tracks / close()

thresholdConfiguration.behaviour: Persistent low-battery warning banner in call UI
Final warning, then automatic call termination
thresholdConfiguration.owningLayer: Client, event reported to Call Service

thresholdConfiguration.behaviour: Same as above with a stricter cut-off for opted-in users

edgeCases.behaviour: Monitoring continues; auto-termination becomes configurable rather than forced, since depletion risk is reduced.
State machine is one-directional per call; a terminated call is never auto-resumed.
Evaluation happens on every ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED broadcast, not a fixed poll interval, so a skipped step still terminates on the next event.
Detected via PowerManager.isPowerSaveMode(); surfaced as a non-blocking advisory (may affect call quality).
Fail open on visibility (never hide the call UI); fail safe on protection (disable auto-termination, show a persistent 'battery protection unavailable' notice).

6_backend_microservices.stack: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3, one deployable per bounded context

communication.synchronous: REST/gRPC between gateway and services, and service-to-service lookups needing an immediate answer
communication.asynchronous: Kafka topics: message.sent, call.started, call.terminated.low_battery, status.published, notification.requested
communication.realtime: WebSocket (STOMP) for chat delivery/presence; dedicated WebSocket signaling channel for WebRTC (offer/answer/ICE)

services.name: API Gateway
services.responsibility: Routing, authn/z, rate limiting, request aggregation

services.name: Auth Service
services.responsibility: Registration, OTP, login, JWT issuance, sessions, 2FA

services.name: Media Service
services.responsibility: Upload/download brokering, transcoding hooks, virus scan

services.name: Call Service
services.responsibility: Call signaling, call state, call history, battery-event log

services.name: Admin Service
services.responsibility: Moderation, reports, abuse detection, analytics dashboards

7_realtime_and_calling_architecture.signalingRole: Call Service brokers SDP offer/answer and ICE candidates over WebSocket; never touches raw audio/video
sequence: Both peers exchange ICE candidates via signaling
Media flows P2P (SRTP) when possible, else relayed via TURN server

infrastructure.role: Exchanges SDP/ICE over WebSocket; tracks call state (ringing, active, ended, ended_low_battery).
Helps each peer discover its public IP/port for direct P2P connectivity.
Relays encrypted media when direct P2P is not possible.
Recommended for group video calls beyond MVP to avoid full-mesh bandwidth cost.

storageStrategy.usedFor: System of record: users, auth, message metadata, calls, groups, status metadata, reports.
Online presence, WebSocket session routing, live call state, rate-limit counters, short-lived OTP codes.
Images, videos, documents, voice messages, profile pictures, status media — accessed via signed URLs only.
Durable event log for delivery guarantees, call lifecycle events (incl. low-battery terminations), analytics ingestion.

8_data_architecture.note: battery_events makes the core USP measurable: every warning and every automatic termination is logged with exact battery percentage and call context, feeding the analytics needed to validate the feature.

9_security_architecture: AuthN: OTP + password with JWT access/refresh tokens; refresh tokens rotated and stored hashed
AuthZ: per-service scope checks at the gateway plus method-level checks in each service
Encryption at rest: PostgreSQL volume encryption, S3 SSE-KMS
End-to-end encryption: 1:1 chat encrypted client-side (Signal-style Double Ratchet); Chat Service stores ciphertext only
Abuse prevention: gateway rate limiting (Redis token bucket), report/block pipeline into Admin Service, automated content flags
Session/device management: multi-device login with per-device session revocation

stack.technology: Docker; one image per microservice, multi-stage builds
GitHub Actions — build, test, scan, push image, deploy
Terraform for VPC, RDS, ECS/EKS, S3, IAM
CloudWatch (logs/metrics), Prometheus + Grafana (dashboards), Sentry/Crashlytics (mobile crash reporting)

11_building_with_google_antigravity.description: Google Antigravity is Google's agent-first development platform (a modified VS Code fork) in which AI agents (Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet, GPT-OSS) plan, write, test, and verify code directly against the Editor, a Terminal, and a Browser, producing reviewable Artifacts instead of opaque diffs.

docs/: architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md  <- this document, source of truth for agents

workspaceLayout.note: Placing docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md at a fixed path lets every agent task reference the architecture as a stable planning input, and lets Antigravity's knowledge base index it once and reuse it across tasks.

skillFiles.purpose: Standard structure for a new Spring Boot microservice: package layout, error-handling convention, health endpoint, Dockerfile, test conventions.
The exact state machine and thresholds from Section 5 — prevents an agent from re-inventing battery logic differently in client vs backend.
Signaling message schema (offer/answer/ICE), call-state enum, required event emissions to Kafka.
Rule: every new endpoint must update its service's OpenAPI spec under docs/api/ before implementation is considered done.
Checklist an agent runs against its own diff before marking a task complete.

steps: Add POST /calls/{id}/battery-events endpoint per docs/api/call-service.yaml (create if missing, per api-contract skill).
Persist to battery_events table (see Section 8 schema).
Emit call.terminated.low_battery to Kafka when event_type=critical.
Write unit tests for all 6 battery test scenarios (see 62_testing_strategy_reference).
Produce an Artifact: test report + sequence diagram matching Section 5's sequence.
Do not modify Auth Service or Chat Service.

verificationArtifacts: Task list / implementation plan Artifact, generated before code is written, checked against Sections 6/7/8
Automated test report Artifact (unit + integration), including the six battery scenarios
For UI-facing work: a browser/emulator screen-recording Artifact of the low-battery warning banner and automatic call termination end-to-end
Architecture-conformance note: which service boundaries, tables, and API contracts were touched

modelSelectionGuidance.taskType: Boilerplate service scaffolding, CRUD endpoints, Terraform modules
modelSelectionGuidance.recommendedModel: Gemini 3 Flash — fast, cheap, high volume

modelSelectionGuidance.taskType: Battery state machine, WebRTC signaling, security-sensitive code, architecture-conformance review
modelSelectionGuidance.recommendedModel: Gemini 3 Pro or Claude Sonnet — higher reasoning depth

modelSelectionGuidance.taskType: Cross-service integration debugging, ambiguous PRD interpretation
modelSelectionGuidance.recommendedModel: Claude Sonnet — strong multi-file reasoning over long structured documents

buildSequence: Open the repo as an Antigravity workspace; index docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md and the PRD into the knowledge base.
Author the SKILL.md files first — they are reused by every later agent.
Run Wave 0 (foundations) as a single Editor-view session (synchronous, low risk).
Switch to the Manager surface for Waves 1-5, launching one agent per service/module in parallel.
Gate every wave on Artifact review before starting the next wave's dependents.
Run Wave 6 as a dedicated verification agent executing the full battery test matrix and success-criteria checklist before Play Store packaging.
